sentences.text:
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Vikram Rajpurohit, Dy.G.A.
 Mr. R.S. Bhati  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE FARJAND ALI Order 13/12/2024 1.
The petitioner has challenged quashing of the entire proceeding pending against the petitioner for accusation of committing offence under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the statutory right given to the accused petitioner could not be availed because of the samples could not be sent to the Central Laboratory before its expiry, and therefore, continuance of further proceeding against the petitioner would be an abuse of process of law.

3. On the contrary, learned counsel for the State would contend that the petitioner can very well agitate the issue before the trial Court at a subsequent stage and it is further contended that there is concurrent finding of two Courts below, therefore, no case is made out in favour of the petitioner.
[2024:RJ-JD:51311] (2 of 3) [CRLMP-4424/2022]
4. Heard learned counsel for both the parties.

entities.text: Ashwani Kumar vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:51311)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is the case of the prosecution that sample of Khoya (Milk- cake) was taken by the Food Inspector by the shop of the petitioner on 31.10.2010 and which was sent to food analyst for examination.

Upon receipt of the report being the food adulterated the officers filed a complaint before the Court on 12.01.2018.
6.

Upon issuance of notices; the petitioner appeared on 01.06.2011 and on the same day he preferred an application under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act seeking further analysis of sample from the Central Laboratory.
For a long time the sample was not produced before the trial Court.
It is revealing that in the year 2015 the samples were sent back because it was in a deteriorated condition.

As a matter of fact, the opportunity to the petitioner to seek for further analysis of the sample before expiry of its shelf life has not been granted or rather he has become deprived of getting the sample re- analyzed by the central laboratory.

7. The law in this regard is not more res integra in light of the judgment passed by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of Girishbhai Dahyabhai Shah Vs. C.C. Jani And Anr. (2009(15) SCC, in which Hon'ble the Supreme Court has propounded that seeking further analysis of the sample is an absolute statutory right of an accused and depriving him from making any prayer in this regard certainly infringes his statutory right and therefore, the proceedings were quashed in the matter.

entities.text: Girishbhai Dahyabhai Shah Vs. C.C. Jani And Anr. (2009(15) SCC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similar is the circumstances here and the case of the petitioner is squarely covered by the judgment referred (supra).
In view of the above, the misc. petition is allowed.

The order dated 21.09.2021 passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Srikaranpur in Criminal Original Case No. 41/2011 as well as the order dated 30.05.2022 passed by the learned Additional Session Judge, Srikaranpur, District Sriganganagar are hereby quashed and set aside and further it is directed that the entire proceeding pending before the trial Court against the petitioner are quashed.

entities.text: Additional Session Judge, Srikaranpur, District Sriganganagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner is exonerated from the charges and his bail bonds shall be canceled.
9. Stay petition stands disposed of.

(FARJAND ALI),J 8-Samvedana/-
